body:
## The Bakersfield Brief — Sunday, August 16, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. We’re starting this Sunday with a heavy heart after a wrong-way crash on Highway 99 left three people dead overnight. It’s shaping up to be a hot one today, with highs near 98° and air quality at a moderate 64. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and what’s ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident was a palm tree fire that spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way in southeast Bakersfield. Fire crews, with Engine 7 taking incident command, worked to contain the blaze as additional units rolled in. No injuries or evacuations were reported on the air. Elsewhere, a serious crash on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road drew a heavy rescue response around 1 a.m. Firefighters extricated two patients from a vehicle that caught fire after a collision, and both were reported walking and stable. 

Around the county, deputies staged on Price Street after a call that began as a report of fireworks escalated to a possible shooting, though no shots were confirmed. A DUI driver in a white BMW fled from the 33rd Street area eastbound around 12:13 a.m., and a vehicle struck a parked car on Myrtle Avenue shortly before 5:40 a.m., prompting a patient assessment. The night also saw multiple calls reporting street racing in the Berkshire area and a long string of low-stakes disturbances, including a domestic incident at a Camellia Village apartment where a hole was punched in the wall.

## Today's weather

Today will be sunny and hot, with a high near 98° and a low tonight around 72°. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL) as of this morning. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64. Stay cool and hydrated if you’re heading outdoors.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early this morning.** According to the California Highway Patrol, a white Honda Accord traveling northbound in the southbound lanes collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado north of 7th Standard Road around 12:44 a.m. The Honda caught fire, and all three occupants died at the scene. The BMW’s driver and one passenger sustained major injuries, while the two occupants of the Chevrolet had minor injuries. CHP is investigating whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 tells us that a man was arrested in a domestic violence standoff in Bakersfield that involved minors.** Bakersfield Police Department said the incident began when officers responded to a domestic disturbance call and found the suspect barricaded inside a residence with children present. After a brief standoff, the man was taken into custody without further incident, and the children were safely removed from the home. The arrest highlights the ongoing challenges local law enforcement faces in handling domestic violence cases that involve vulnerable family members.

**Bakersfield Now announced that the 90s are back as a third heatwave grips Bakersfield, though a Pacific trough is expected to bring slightly cooler highs.** After a brief respite, temperatures are climbing again, with forecasters predicting another round of 90-degree days. However, a cooling trend is on the horizon, with a Pacific trough set to move in and lower temperatures by a few degrees. Residents are advised to stay prepared for hot conditions and to check on vulnerable neighbors during the heat.

## Something good

A Kern County homeless recovery leader is helping to shape a national addiction toolkit aimed at addressing treatment within the homeless community. Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, was among a select group of professionals who worked with federal agencies to develop the toolkit, which outlines best practices for long-term recovery programs. This effort not only benefits our local community but also contributes to a nationwide effort to support individuals struggling with addiction.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar this week. The Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee will meet on Tuesday, August 18, at 12:00 p.m. The Planning Commission will convene on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. Also on Tuesday, the Historic Preservation Commission will meet at 4:00 p.m., followed by the Water Board on Wednesday, August 19, at 10:00 a.m. The Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission will meet on Tuesday, August 18, at 2:00 p.m.

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup. Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los Caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform on August 22. Comedian Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27, followed by Cumbiatron: The Cumbia Rave on August 28. Willie Barcena will perform on August 29, and a Michael Jackson tribute show featuring Michael Phoenix will also be held on August 29. Rounding out the month, the Mi Historia Tour featuring Leyendas del Mariachi USA will be at the Fox Theater on September 4.

That’s your Sunday brief. Stay cool, drive safely, and have a great week ahead.
